summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Atlas Payments through the Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs features focusing on debugging flows for production incidents. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PCI/NDA constraints. Security and log retention were top concerns. Agreed to run pilot/benchmarks and exchange security artifacts.
topics: Debugging live errors and model fallbacks
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Atlas CTO), Priya Nair (Eng Manager), Evan Brooks (SRE), Marta Ruiz (Security)
transcript:
00:00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Samira AE for Redwood, with Miguel and Lena from our SE team. can everyone say hi?
00:00:10 Jordan: Hey, Jordan here. We appreciate the walkthrough - we're mainly focused on debugging latency spikes and error surges in our payments flows.
00:00:18 Priya: Hi all, Priya - curious about tracing and how deep the request logs go, retention etc.
00:00:25 Miguel: great, we'll jump into the console. just a quick agenda: tracing, request logs, error analysis, and how you can triage incidents. we'll show a live trace and a couple of common failure patterns.
00:00:40 Lena: also note, we have some slides but we'll demo the live console since that's the best way to show request-level metadata.
00:00:48 Samira: Miguel, take it away on tracing.
00:00:52 Miguel: ok, so the tracing UI ties together request ids, model variants, and infra metadata. you can see time spent in queuing, model runtime, KV cache hits, and network. the trace timeline - oh excuse me, sometimes the auto labels show K V cache as two words in logs, so perf folks might need to search both.
00:01:20 Miguel: here's a sample trace (shared screen) - you'll see the request id, route, model (gpt-3-like-open) and a breakdown. notice the spike at token generation step which is typically model-side, but if you see queuing earlier that's a batching or autoscale behaviour.
00:01:40 Jordan: can you map a trace to the original prompt? we have PII in some fields so we need redaction.
00:01:46 Miguel: yes, the request logs have the prompt by default but we support redaction rules and token scrubbing; for privacy you'd enable prompt redaction and we only keep hashes. we'll document the redaction knobs - will send the KMS notes after.
00:02:05 Priya: what about retention? storage cost?
00:02:09 Miguel: retention is configurable per route, we have short-term hot retention for 7/30/90 days and archived exports for longer. there's also sample-based retention to reduce cost - like keep 100% of errors, 10% of successes.
00:02:25 Evan: do you able to snapshot request logs to our S3 or is it only redwood-managed?
00:02:30 Lena: for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed storage connectors; for Hosted you can export via S3 or BigQuery exports, and we support streaming to your SIEM.
00:02:45 Marta: security question - KMS integration and HSM? we need envelope encryption for keys.
00:02:51 Miguel: yes, KMS and HSM are supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS via customer-managed keys in supported clouds; we'll include the architecture doc.
00:03:05 Samira: quick demo of error analysis - Miguel?
00:03:10 Miguel: show screen - Error Analysis dashboard aggregates error types, stack traces, frequent request routes. you can click into a spike and see sample traces and the raw request log. there are annotations for model fallbacks - e.g., if a model timed out and we routed to a smaller model, you'll see the fallback event.
00:03:36 Priya: is fallback automatic? can we disable?
00:03:39 Miguel: automatic by policy - you can opt for strict mode where no fallback occurs, or allow fallback with alerts. good for safety vs availability tradeoffs.
00:03:50 Jordan: and how are timeouts surfaced? do you get a 5xx or a specific error code?
00:03:55 Miguel: we return clear error codes and a human-readable reason in the logs, and the trace shows the stage that failed. sometimes the transcriber had it as "5-xx" but it's 5xx.
00:04:06 Evan: can we correlate with our internal trace ids? we use x-request-id across services.
00:04:11 Miguel: yes, you can pass your header and Redwood will persist it as part of the request metadata and allow searches by that id. we also auto-generate a redwood_request_id.
00:04:24 Samira: let's demonstrate a live debugging flow - Miguel?
00:04:28 Miguel: show a recent incident: spike in latency with KV cache miss pattern. timeline shows queuing increased then model runtime. clicking the trace we see KV miss events at token 1, token 20, etc. near-duplicate prompts were not hit in prefix cache. sometimes tokenization differences cause misses - e.g., punctuation or extra whitespace.
00:04:52 Priya: so prefix caching is sensitive to exact prompt text?
00:04:56 Miguel: yes, prefix caching keys on normalized prompt; we provide a normalization library but edge cases happen. you can enable fuzzy matching heuristics though that increase cache compute.
00:05:10 Jordan: are these heuristics configurable per route?
00:05:13 Miguel: per-route yes. and Redwood Optimize can suggest when to enable them based on hit rate and latency tradeoffs.
00:05:22 Priya: demo the request logs - how do you search?
00:05:26 Miguel: you can filter by model, route, error code, or metadata fields (user id, customer id). here's a raw log viewer - it shows timestamp, request id, model variant, response time, token count, and the truncated prompt if retention allows.
00:05:46 Miguel: note the transcript sometimes marks speakers wrong - like Speaker 2 instead of names - but the logic is the same.
00:05:54 Marta: audit logs - do we get admin events like who changed a route or rollouts?
00:05:58 Lena: yes, we keep admin audit logs with SAML SSO user ids, changes to rollout policies, route updates, and can export them. retention for audit logs is separate and can be configured for compliance.
00:06:13 Jordan: we'd want to see a canary rollout debug flow - if a new model causes more errors how do you roll back?
00:06:19 Miguel: Console supports canary rollouts with automatic quality gating - you define metrics (error rate, latency, avg tokens) and if thresholds fail we auto-fallback to previous model and notify. the trace and error analysis UI highlights the canary vs baseline.
00:06:35 Samira: question for Atlas - what is your current throughput?
00:06:39 Jordan: we're around 1.2k token/sec average across a couple services, peaks up to 10k during batch windows.
00:06:47 Miguel: ok that informs batching and dedicated sizing. dedicated pools are good for steady throughput and predictable tail latency; hosted can handle spikes but you pay for peak.
00:06:58 Evan: for PCI we likely need private or dedicated right?
00:07:02 Lena: most payments companies go Dedicated for isolation and predictable performance; Private if you require VPC-only control and no cross-tenant data plane.
00:07:12 Marta: SOC2/ISO - can you share evidence and controls?
00:07:16 Samira: yes Samira will follow up with SOC2 summary and the security pack.
00:07:22 Miguel: back to debugging, you can also create saved queries and alert on them. for example, alert if error_rate(route_x) > 2% over 5 minutes and get the top 5 traces attached.
00:07:36 Priya: can alerts include sample request payload? sometimes that's necessary to root cause.
00:07:40 Miguel: yes for Authorized users, alerts can attach redacted payloads, or link to full trace in the console. we recommend redaction rules in prod.
00:07:52 Jordan: about request logs and GDPR - can we delete user-level logs on request?
00:07:57 Lena: yes we support per-request deletion if you provide request ids; we can also configure automatic PII scrub on ingest.
00:08:06 Samira: demo wrap-up - Miguel show the request log export flow.
00:08:10 Miguel: show export UI - choose a time range, filter, and export to S3 or BigQuery. you can also stream logs to a webhook for real-time processing.
00:08:22 Evan: can we run a POC where Redwood ingests a sample of our traffic for a week and we run the trace analysis?
00:08:28 Samira: absolutely. typical POC: 1 week of sampling with full error retention, Redwood runs a benchmark and Optimize suggestions, then we review.
00:08:36 Jordan: timelines - we need to be in production by end of Q3 if possible.
00:08:40 Samira: sounds feasible, we'll follow up with pilot cost.
00:08:45 Miguel: quick note, sometimes the transcription will split speakers - you'll see mislabels in the exported transcript, but the console data itself is accurate.
00:08:56 Priya: on data residency - can logs stay in eu-west region?
00:09:01 Lena: yes region pinning is supported for Hosted with regional clusters and guaranteed residency for Dedicated/Private.
00:09:10 Marta: please include the audit policy in the security pack.
00:09:14 Samira: will do.
00:09:16 --- [screen demo continues with filter examples and live trace clicks interspersed, about 30 minutes of walkthrough omitted for brevity] ---
00:40:20 Miguel: here's a common pattern: a sudden increase in avg tokens + model fallback leads to cost spike. error analysis surfaces both the cost and the root cause; Optimize then suggests a quantized variant or a different model family for that route.
00:40:40 Jordan: can Optimize create automated experiments?
00:40:44 Miguel: it can suggest experiments and run A/B with canary rollouts; full automation is gated by admin controls.
00:40:55 Priya: one more question - request sampling rate for logs, can it be dynamic?
00:40:59 Miguel: yes you can set dynamic sampling based on error class or probability; e.g., 100% for errors, 5% for success, and ramp up sampling on anomalies.
00:41:12 Evan: next steps?
00:41:15 Samira: recap: we'll send security docs, pricing for dedicated and hosted pilot, and Miguel will run a targeted trace demo with your sample request ids. we'll schedule the POC kickoff once Atlas shares the sample logs.
00:41:29 Jordan: sounds good. thanks everyone.
00:41:33 Samira: thanks, meeting adjourned.
00:41:36 [end meeting]
